title: Pushing the Limits of Off Axis Electron Holography for the Quantitative Mapping of Electromagnetic Fields
content: Given the current interest in 4D STEM based techniques, off-axis electron holography is seen as a rather old fashioned or maybe forgotten about method for measuring electromagnetic fields [1]. I will discuss how state of the art off-axis electron holography is being used today for quantitative mapping of electrostatic fields for advanced materials science applications [2]. After 20 years of development at CEA LETI it has become a mature technique that is used daily to contribute towards the development of electronic devices. We will discuss hologram-summing techniques for improving signal to noise, reconstruction methods for improving spatial resolution, quantification and interpretation of data, dealing with artefacts as well as best practices for specimen preparation for static and in-situ biasing observations [3].
